noAddresses: No network addresses: devices cannot reach the server.
mdnsDown: Not published: devices connect by IP address
notListening: Devices cannot connect: the server cannot open its UDP port. The log, server.log in the server folder, says why; the server keeps trying.
udpWarning: Changing the UDP port means every device must pair again.
httpHint: After a change, this page opens at the new port.
confirmUdpText: Every paired device remembers the port, so every device will have to pair again.
noApps: No apps yet. Add one below.
appIdHint: Lowercase Latin letters, digits and hyphens, up to 64. It cannot be changed later.
appNameHint: Shown on this page. If empty, the ID is used.
idInvalid: Use only lowercase Latin letters, digits and hyphens, 1 to 64 of them.
deleteText: The app leaves the list, its folder with the document and every saved version is deleted, and its devices are disconnected and removed.
removeText: The device loses access. To sync again, it must pair again.
pairIntro: On the device, open the app's sync settings and scan this code, or paste its text.
pairRules: A code works for one device, for 10 minutes. A new code cancels the previous one.
qrAlt: The pairing code as a QR code
copyFailed: Could not copy. The text is selected: copy it by hand.
expired: The code has expired. Press “New code”.
refused: A device tried to pair the app {app}, which this server does not serve yet.
addedRetry: Added. Now pair the device again.
dataDirHint: Where the apps' documents and versions are kept. A folder that does not exist yet is created.
moveText: The current data of the apps below will be moved to the new folder, and the server restarts.
adoptTitle: Use the data in this folder?
adoptText: This folder already holds data of the apps below. It becomes the current data, and the server restarts.
errDataExists: This folder already holds data of a workspace-server. Choose another folder, or delete that data first.
errDataChanged: The folder changed meanwhile. Try again.
errBusy: The server is already being changed. Wait until the page reloads.
restartFailed: The server did not come back. Look at server.log in the server folder.
restartError: The last restart did not finish: {error}
manageIntro: Stop the server here, or delete what it stores. Nothing is deleted until you confirm.
deleteServerButton: Delete the server and all data
stopText: The server stops and no longer starts at login. Your data is kept. To start it again, run “workspace-server start” in a terminal or open the program file.
resetText: The server starts over as if it were new: the documents and versions of every app, the list of apps and the paired devices are deleted, and every device must pair again. The name, the ports and the data folder are kept. It cannot be undone.
deleteServerTitle: Delete the server and all data?
deleteServerText: The server stops and is removed completely: it no longer starts at login, and everything it stored is deleted, together with its folders and the program file below. Every device must pair again with a new server. It cannot be undone.
stoppedText: You can close this tab. To start the server again, run “workspace-server start” in a terminal or open the program file.
stoppedDeletedText: The server has stopped and is being removed together with its data and program file. You can close this tab.
errExists: An app with this ID already exists.
errConfirmMismatch: The typed ID does not match.
errNotFound: Not found: it may have been removed already.
errForbidden: The server refused the request. Open the page at its own address.
errInternal: Something went wrong on the server.
errNetwork: The server cannot be reached. Is it running?
numberRange: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.
upstreamMainIntro: This server is a main: devices pair with it. It can instead be linked to another main as its subordinate, as a laptop's server is linked to the PC's: it then keeps a copy of the main's apps on this computer, and devices paired with the main sync with it whenever the main is out of reach.
upstreamHasSubordinates: Other servers are linked to this one (see Devices), so it cannot be linked to another main. To link it, remove them first.
linkHow: Get a pairing code from the main: on its page, Devices → “Pair a device”, or from a phone paired with it. Paste the code here, or scan its QR code with this computer's camera.
linkDataNote: Nothing is deleted. Where both servers already hold an app's document, the main's copy wins here, this server's is kept among the saved versions, and the devices merge the two.
scanning: Hold the main's QR code in front of the camera.
cameraFailed: The camera is not available. Paste the code instead.
connectingText: The main is out of reach now. This server keeps trying, and devices sync with it meanwhile.
haltedRemoved: The main removed this server. Unlink it; to link it again, it needs a new code.
haltedNotMain: The server at the main's address is no longer a main. Unlink this server, then link it to the main.
haltedServerChanged: Another server answers at the main's addresses. Unlink this server, then link it again with the main's code.
haltedTooOld: The main does not understand this server. Update the main, then restart this server.
haltedOther: The link stopped. A restart of this server tries again.
stoppedAppsText: These apps wrote to the main more than 10 times within a minute, so they stopped syncing with it, to keep the saved versions on both servers. Their devices still sync with this server. “Resume” syncs an app with the main again at once; a restart of this server resumes them all. An app that keeps writing that often stops again.
stoppedAppsHaltedText: These apps wrote to the main more than 10 times within a minute, so they stopped syncing with it, to keep the saved versions on both servers. Their devices still sync with this server. A restart of this server resumes them.
resumedLater: {app} syncs with the main again as soon as the main is in reach.
resumeNotStopped: That app is not stopped any more.
inviteIntro: This is a pairing code of the main server, {name}. In a browser on this computer, open the app's sync settings and paste it; a phone can scan it too. The device pairs with the main, and syncs with this server whenever the main is out of reach.
inviteRules: A code works for one device, for 10 minutes. A new code cancels the previous one, including the one on the main's page.
inviteUnreachable: The main server cannot be reached now, and only it issues pairing codes. Try again when this computer and the main are on the same network.
unlinkText: This server stops syncing with the main and becomes a main again. No data is deleted: the apps and their documents stay here, and everything on the main stays there. The main's devices can no longer sync through this server.
unlinked: Unlinked. This server is a main again.
unlinkedNotTold: Unlinked. The main could not be reached, so it still lists this server: remove it on the main's page, under Devices.
linkInvalidCode: This is not a pairing code of another workspace-server.
linkBusy: A link is being made or undone. Wait a moment.
linkNotLinked: This server is not linked to a main server.
linkHasSubordinates: Other servers are linked to this one: remove them under Devices first.
linkBadSecret: The code is used or has expired. Get a new code from the main.
linkBlocked: The main refuses this computer for a few minutes after too many failed attempts. Try again later.
linkNotMain: That server is itself linked to another one. Use the code of the main server.
linkServerChanged: Another server answers at that code's addresses.
linkUnreachable: The main server cannot be reached. Is it running, and on the same network as this computer?
linkTooOld: The main server is too old for this. Update it first.
subordinateDevices: This server is linked to the main server {name}: devices pair with the main, which hands this server out to them. Pair a phone on the main's page; pair the browser on this computer here.
removeServerText: The server on that computer stops syncing with this one, and devices no longer sync through it. Its data stays there. To link it again, it needs a new code.
errNotMain: This server is linked to a main server: devices pair with the main.
serversIntro: Each keeps a copy of this server's apps, and devices paired here sync with it whenever this server is out of reach.
promoteText: The documents are made the same on both servers first. Then this server becomes the main: the current main hands its role over and syncs through this server, and so do the other servers linked to it. Devices follow by themselves, without pairing again. Nothing is deleted.
promoted: This server is the main now, and {name} syncs through it.
promotedNotFollowed: This server is the main now. {name} has not followed yet: it does as soon as this server reaches it.
promoteForceTitle: {name} is out of reach. Make this server the main anyway?
promoteForceText: This server becomes the main now, without asking the main. If the main still runs, both act as main until they meet: devices sync with whichever one they reach, and nothing is lost. When the two meet, the one made main later wins: the old main steps down by itself and syncs through this server. If the old main is gone for good, this is how the others go on without it.
promotedForced: This server is the main now. The old main steps down when the two meet; the other servers follow when this server reaches them.
promoteNotInStep: The documents are not yet the same on this server and the main. Try again in a moment.
mainSteppedDownText: The main handed its role to another server. This server is looking for the new main among the servers linked to it, and links to it by itself.
waitingText: This server took over as the main. These servers follow it as soon as it reaches them:
waitingRemoveText: A server that is gone for good can be removed under Devices.
handOverText: The documents are made the same on both servers first. Then that server becomes the main: this one hands its role over and syncs through it, and so do the other linked servers. Devices follow by themselves, without pairing again. Nothing is deleted.
handedOver: {name} is the main now; this server syncs through it.
handOverPending: {name} was asked to take the role over. This server follows it as soon as it has.
handOverNotConnected: That server is not connected now. Hand the role over while it is.
